tool.name: passive_dns_history
tool.description:
Mine passive-DNS history for historical resolutions and known subdomains.
Surfaces stale subdomains that don't currently resolve but historically pointed somewhere (defunct cloud projects, internal infra leaked into public passive-DNS feeds). Often the highest-value finding source on a domain target — pair the discovered subdomains with `subdomain_takeover_check` to flag dangling CNAMEs.
Provider keys (set in the worker environment): - `STRIX_SECURITYTRAILS_KEY` — preferred (direct historical-A endpoint). - `STRIX_VIRUSTOTAL_KEY` — fallback (free-tier-friendlier).
Fails open when no keys are configured — returns success=False with error_reason="no api keys configured" and a hint. The agent should move on to other recon tools.
Doesn't emit findings on its own — historical-DNS data is informational. Subsequent tools should consume the discovered subdomains.

parameter.name: domain
parameter.description: Apex or subdomain to query (e.g. "example.com" or "app.example.com").

parameter.name: prefer
parameter.description: "securitytrails" or "virustotal". When set and the key is available, that provider is queried alone. When unset, falls back to whichever key(s) are configured.

returns.description:
{success, domain, providers_queried, results: [...], merged_resolutions, merged_subdomains, merged_subdomain_count}.
Each entry in `results` has the per-provider raw response; `merged_resolutions` is a unified `[{ip, first_seen?, last_seen, type}]` list across providers; `merged_subdomains` is the deduped sorted list of subdomains observed.
